text: I think it's partly because of fashion. People want to show that they have the latest model, and new phones often have better cameras and faster speeds. Also, advertising is very powerful, so people feel that their old device is not good enough anymore. Personally, I try not to follow trends too much, because I'd rather spend my money on something more useful, like travelling.

text: In some ways, yes. For example, many people use their phones to calculate even simple numbers, so their memory and thinking skills may get weaker. Navigation apps also mean that people don't learn the streets in their own city. On the other hand, gadgets save time, and that time can be used for more important things. So it depends on how people use them.

text: I'm not sure it's a good idea for very young children. They might spend too many hours watching videos, which is bad for their eyes and their concentration. On the other hand, some educational apps can teach them letters and numbers. I think parents should set clear time limits, maybe one hour a day, and use the device together with the child.

text: Many old devices just end up in landfills, which is a real problem because they contain harmful materials like lead. Some people keep them in drawers, and others throw them away. I think companies should take responsibility by offering recycling programmes, for example, giving a discount if you return your old phone. That way, valuable metals can be reused instead of wasted.
